title: Content Evaluation: a recorded missing-Process revision

steps.title: Inspect Process discovery and its archive version
steps.question: Is this discovery file a before-state?
steps.look: The discovery archive already lists magnetic separation. Later in this guide, compare it with the revision prompt, which records an empty Process design.
steps.boundary: Files have different update times. Do not treat today's discovery record as the pre-revision state.

steps.title: Find the missing Process
steps.question: Why can this PCB not be a HAS_OUTPUT subject?
steps.look: The request retains a draft phone PCB → HAS_OUTPUT → Fe, 76%. Section 2.2 identifies magnetic separation as the treatment.
steps.boundary: This MPPCBs draft is unresolved, not an accepted KG fact. Its evidence supports a missing Process.

steps.title: Inspect the committed operation
steps.question: What did Process Revision add?
steps.look: The recorded add_process operation names magnetic separation and references three candidates: MPPCBs, CPCBs and FPCBs. Its run status is committed.
steps.boundary: Request and evidence IDs connect the records. This is an archived operation, not a new model call.

steps.title: Check the result and its limits
steps.question: Was every issue resolved?
steps.look: One LLM call committed one operation: three requests approved and six relations rebound. Three outputs still lack structured Settings.
steps.boundary: Resolving a missing Process does not automatically resolve its Settings.

steps.title: Attach post-merge sample scope
steps.question: Which merged sample does the Fe observation describe?
steps.look: Scope describes the batch of mobile-phone PCBs (MPPCBs). In the current pipeline this provenance pass follows document merge and Process revision, before final export.
steps.boundary: Scope does not perform the missing-Process repair. Separate archive versions do not establish a continuous historical run.

steps.title: Keep the PCB as the input
steps.question: How is the original sample preserved?
steps.look: The final input is phone PCB → PROCESSED_BY → magnetic separation. The PCB remains a Component.
steps.boundary: The correction adds a treatment bridge, not a new sample identity or Process hierarchy.

steps.title: Preserve the 76% Fe observation
steps.question: What changed, and what stayed the same?
steps.look: Magnetic separation → HAS_OUTPUT → Fe keeps 76%, sample MPPCBs and the original evidence. Its binding request points back to the unresolved Relation request.
steps.boundary: The subject changed to a Process; the material, value and source did not.

steps.title: Keep the 84% observation separate
steps.question: Does one shared Process imply one shared recovery value?
steps.look: Computer PCBs retain 84% Fe under the same Process, with a different sample group and binding request.
steps.boundary: Relation IDs are reused; value and provenance distinguish observations. No average is computed.

steps.title: Show the 28% result and missing 54%
steps.question: Are all four percentages in the source represented?
steps.look: Fax PCBs retain 28% Fe. The source also reports 54% for COPCBs, absent from this frozen final output.
steps.boundary: A committed revision is not complete extraction coverage. The demo does not fill this gap.

steps.title: Inspect the corrected Process bridge
steps.question: Can graph observations return to their requests?
steps.look: Magnetic separation connects PCB inputs to separate 76%, 84% and 28% Fe observations. View evidence in replay follows their binding requests.
steps.boundary: Known gaps remain: no 54% COPCBs result and three missing Settings. This is not a new evaluation.
